optimization.action_description: Add an in-repo CUDA extension path that converts TRT-LLM PackedScoreIdx<bf16> top-k routing into the MoE grouped-GEMM metadata consumed by FlashInfer/TensorRT-LLM: expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx, permuted_idx_to_token_idx, cta_idx_xy_to_batch_idx, cta_idx_xy_to_mn_limit, num_non_exiting_ctas, total_num_padded_tokens, and expert counts/offsets.
optimization.implementation: Use chunk-parallel deterministic rank generation. Each 256-slot chunk computes in-chunk ranks and per-expert counts, a per-expert prefix over chunks produces global ranks, and scatter adds padded expert offsets to match FlashInfer's expert-major permuted token order.
optimization.expected_impact: This creates the correct metadata contract needed to replace the current scalar FP4 stage kernels with a TensorRT-LLM-style grouped GEMM path. It does not yet make the full candidate faster than FlashInfer.

correctness.reference: probe_routing_metadata.py Python reproduction of FlashInfer block routing rules for PackedScoreIdx<bf16>

performance.comparison_to_previous_ordered_rank: The first deterministic single-block rank implementation passed correctness but measured about 1023.68 us on full G11 metadata. The chunk-parallel implementation reduced full G11 metadata latency to about 151.94 us while preserving zero mismatches.

quality_gate.reason: The routing metadata contract is now correct and reasonably cheap, but the end-to-end candidate still uses scalar/software FP4 stage1/stage2 kernels and remains slower than flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe.

next_step.description: Use the validated metadata to drive a grouped/tiled FP4 GEMM path for stage1, followed by SwiGLU+NVFP4 quantization and grouped stage2 finalize/scatter. The next proof point should replace one scalar stage with a tensor-core path without calling flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe.
